newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Top Glory to issue fewer shrs for hotels.
newsitem.headline: Top Glory to issue fewer shrs for hotels.

text.p: Top Glory International Holdings Ltd said it would issue fewer-than-planned shares to parent Top Glory Holding Co Ltd (TGH) to fund the purchase of four hotels from TGH, making up the difference with a loan.
Top Glory said in a statement it would settle part of its HK$1.0 billion purchase of hotel interests in China from TGH by issue of 206.03 million new shares at HK$1.63 each.

A further HK$580 million would be paid in cash, with the balance of HK$84.46 million to be a loan repayable to TGH on the first anniversary of the date of completion of the deal together with interest.
The company had originally planned to issue 257.85 million new shares to TGH and pay HK$580 million in cash.
Top Glory said the decision was made after TGH withdrew a general offer waiver application in relation to the new share issue from the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC).

The application was withdrawn because a required independent valuation of all Top Glory's property interests would not be completed in time to avoid delay in despatch of a circular to Top Glory shareholders detailing the hotels deal, it said.

Top Glory said such a delay would not be in the interest of shareholders and, based on the recommendation of its independent financial adviser, a valuation would not have substantially affected the voting preference of independent shareholders.

On completion of the hotels deal, TGH's stake in Top Glory would rise to 45.95 percent from 41.56 percent, with the increase less than the five percent "creeper limit" that would trigger a general offer.
Under the original plan to issue 257.85 million shares, TGH's stake in Top Glory would have risen to 47.07 percent from 41.56 percent.
Top Glory shares were down HK$0.01 late Wednesday morning at HK$1.58.
